correctness.rationale: For any connected graph the inverse M-matrix gives positive off-diagonals. The Loewner comparison with complete-graph Laplacian proves diagonal lower bounds. A PSD inverse-difference integral proves equality on a vertex exactly if no complement edges touch it, i.e. it is universal. The exact diagonal bound crosses one half at h=2/(N-2), strictly above for all other vertices. Continuity and long-step limit imply strict larger thresholds in graphs without universal vertices. At least one universal vertex gives a negative diagonal immediately beyond the bound. Exact rational checker verified 830 connected/sampled cases; infinite proof does not rely on samples.

value.rationale: Determines a sharp graph-order uniform positivity guarantee over the entire class of connected N-vertex networks and characterizes every extremizer by universal vertices. This is an actionable bound when internal topology is uncertain, and a structural rigidity principle independent of all edges between neighbors. The equality case and arbitrary-graph scope are mathematically motivated, rather than an arbitrary small-graph table or numerical threshold fitting.
